seal.statement: A services row whose address is not a unified address must not raise an untyped failure in peer admission. Quest learner-host-from-committed-admission made the admission derive the committed node by parsing the row's address, and on PR #184's gate 41482547014 a row with address ws://localhost:<port>/partition/<id> threw MalformedAddressError out of the reconcile setImmediate hop (test/integration/services-p1-self-referential-write.integration.test.js), where main answers a typed outcome. An unparsable address now resolves to no node, so the admission reaches the port's one typed refusal for an ADD that names no node (RAFT_MEMBERSHIP_CHANGE_REFUSAL.WITHOUT_NODE_ID), reconcile treats it as unadmitted and records it, for the partition and the message group alike; a founding cohort with such a row records no node for that founder instead of throwing.

text: Can a production services row carry an address that is not a unified address? Yes, it is reachable though no ordinary owner writes one. The ordinary writers write unified addresses: partition-service-row-owner.js and partition-service-lifecycle-methods.js write service.unifiedAddress, replica-handler-status-methods.js writes buildTrackedServiceAddress, and ws:// addresses go to the separate endpoints table (node-registration-owner-publication-methods.js:264, bootstrap-request-owner.js:159), not services. But nothing enforces it: services.address is unconstrained TEXT (system-table-core-schema-definitions.js:260) and bootstrap-api-registration-methods.js:117 copies serviceData.address verbatim from the /register-service request with no format check I could find; the system-table insert path used by test/integration/services-p1-self-referential-write.integration.test.js:362 is the same. So a row is a projection a caller can make malformed, and 82 test files write a ws:// address. Not measured on a live cluster.

Census of parses of a row-derived address added by the transplant (git diff origin/main...HEAD -- src, getNodeId, parse, getServiceId, getServiceType): exactly three. (1) admitPartitionRaftPeer, row address from resolvePeerAddressFromService. (2) message-group-service-raft-lifecycle.js reconcileRaftPeersFromCache, row address from peerAddressOfServiceRow. (3) sql-query-engine-provision-target-methods.js founderNodeIdsOf, row address at line 363; awaited, so a rejected CREATE TABLE rather than an uncaught throw, but still untyped. All three are repaired.

Design: AddressManager.nodeIdOfProjectedAddress (built on the existing non-throwing validate) gives null for an address that is not unified. Admission then reaches the port's existing refusal of an ADD that names no node (raft-rs-operation-port.js:161, RAFT_MEMBERSHIP_CHANGE_REFUSAL.WITHOUT_NODE_ID), which admitGroupPeer records as REFUSED at warn, and reconcile treats REFUSED as unadmitted. No new outcome. A follower and an existing member keep NOT_LEADER and ALREADY_MEMBER because the port is reached only where a proposal is made. Consequence of the refusal: the next change to the row re-runs reconcile, so a corrected row admits the peer (witnessed on a real port). A founder with such a row commits no node, and addressing it refuses typed. Rejected: reading the row's node_id column (coordinator ruling: swaps one row input for another; Group B's work removes row addressing).

Added AddressManager.nodeIdOfProjectedAddress; admitPartitionRaftPeer and the message-group reconcile use it instead of getNodeId; founderNodeIdsOf skips an address validate refuses. Witnesses test/partition/peer-admission-unparsable-address.test.js (real leader through the real port, follower, founding cohort) and test/message-group/message-group-unparsable-peer-address.test.js. Red before the change: both partition admission tests and the message-group test failed with MalformedAddressError; the founder test first failed on a fixture error, then proved red by mutation (restoring the unguarded parse gives MalformedAddressError). Base eba822874d5baf59c9342365474f17a063e753a7.
